findings.passage: “Many voters were very upset after the 2020 election and they want lawmakers to take steps to enhance public trust in the electoral system,” Flood said. “People want to know for sure that the person in office is the one who legitimately won the election.”
findings.note: Quote in a House caucus release on House passage of House Bill 1300 (election reform bill she co-sponsored). The release describes the bill as requiring ID from voters, and last-four Social Security or driver's licence numbers for mail-in and absentee ballot applications.

findings.passage: “We want to ensure elections are fair and the outcomes reflect the will of the people who legally cast their ballots,” Flood said. “This has been one of the top issues for people I’ve talked with in our district since I took office back in January.”
findings.note: Second quote in the same release, on why she backed the election reform bill.

House Bill 1300, election reform: release says she co-sponsored it. It would require voters to show one of many acceptable forms of ID (including a free county voter registration card) and require a driver's licence or Social Security digits on mail-in and absentee ballot applications.
